speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; please tell me, when did these symptoms first start?

Also, does the pain or numbness radiate from your neck into the arm, or is it isolated to the arm itself?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning. Given your history of diabetes, steroid use, and significant weight loss, we need to rule out serious underlying causes like malignancy or metabolic neuropathy. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR). REQUEST TEST: Right Arm Nerve Conduction Studies and Electromyography (EMG). REQUEST TEST: Chest X-Ray and Abdominal CT scan.

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing right brachial plexus involvement.

The imaging reveals a mass at the apex of your right lung, which explains your weakness, sensory loss, and the radiating pain typical of nerve compression in this location. Given your history of smoking and weight loss, we must proceed immediately with a biopsy to confirm malignancy and determine the specific cancer type.
